Write ONE test file `/root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/test/server.smoke.test.mjs` (node:test + node:assert/strict, Node v22 built-ins only, ES module, no npm installs) that black-box tests `/root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/server.mjs` by spawning `node server.mjs` as a child process. Do NOT edit server.mjs; if a test fails because of a server bug, keep the test (it must reflect the spec), and report the failure with details in your final message. Read the spec at `/root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23/.team/notes/spec.md` (sections "Server", "API", "Booking rules") — that is the source of truth for every message and status. Data file layout is `{"nextId": <int>, "bookings": [...]}`.

Project rules: no console.log; small focused helper functions (<50 lines); keep the file under ~450 lines; each test creates its own temp dir via fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(),'booking-')) and removes it after; never leave child processes running (kill in t.after / finally).

Helpers to write:
- `startServer({env, cwd})`: spawn process.execPath with [absolute path of server.mjs], env = {...process.env, PORT:'0', DATA_FILE:<tmp>/data.json, ...env}; resolve with {port, child} when stdout emits the line matching /^listening on http:\/\/127\.0\.0\.1:(\d+)\n$/; reject if it exits first (include stderr).
- `runToExit({env, cwd})`: resolve {code, stdout, stderr} when the process exits (timeout 5s).
- `request(port, method, path, {headers, body})` using node:http (NOT fetch — fetch normalizes paths) with `path` sent raw; returns {status, headers, text, json (parsed or undefined)}.

Test cases:
1. Startup errors: PORT='abc', PORT='65536', PORT='-1', PORT=' 80' → exit 1, one stderr line, empty stdout. PORT in use (start a net server on 127.0.0.1:0 first, pass its port) → exit 1, empty stdout. DATA_FILE pointing to a directory → exit 1, stderr exactly `cannot read data file <value as given>\n`; same for empty file, `not json`, `[]`, `{"nextId":1}`. Use a relative DATA_FILE (e.g. 'sub' with cwd = tmp dir where sub is a dir) for one case to check the name is echoed as given. PORT invalid AND data file invalid → stderr is about PORT (does not contain 'cannot read data file'), proving order.
2. Missing data file (ENOENT, including a missing folder) → starts, GET /api/bookings → {bookings:[]}, and the file is NOT created by startup or GETs.
3. stdout is exactly the listening line; with PORT=0 the port is a real number > 0.
4. Routing: GET /api/rooms → 200 {"rooms":["Aurora","Borealis","Cosmos"]} with content-type exactly `application/json; charset=utf-8`. 404 `{"error":"not found"}` for /api/%62ookings, /api/./rooms, /API/rooms, /api/bookings/, /api/bookings/1/, /nope (with GET and POST). 405 `{"error":"method not allowed"}` for GET /api/bookings/abc, PUT /api/rooms, POST /api/rooms, OPTIONS /api/bookings, DELETE /api/bookings, POST /. HEAD /api/rooms → 405 status. Query ignored: GET /api/rooms?x=1 → 200.
5. DELETE: /api/bookings/abc, /api/bookings/0, /api/bookings/01, /api/bookings/999 → 404 `booking not found`; create then DELETE /api/bookings/1 → 204, empty body, then 404 on repeat.
6. Booking rules in order (POST /api/bookings), each asserting exact status and error: missing content-type → 415; `text/plain` → 415; ` APPLICATION/JSON \t; charset=x` is accepted; 415 wins over a too-large body; body of 10001 bytes with JSON content type → 413 (client actually receives the reply); a 10000-byte valid object padded with whitespace is NOT 413; bodies '', 'null', '[]', '"s"', '1', 'true', '{bad', and BOM-prefixed '﻿{}' → 400 `body must be a JSON object`; room 'aurora' / missing → 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos`; title '   ' / 81 chars / number → 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters`; title '  hi  ' stored as 'hi'; 80 chars after trim OK; date '2026-11-3', ' 2026-11-03', '2100-01-01', '1999-12-31', '2026-02-29', '2026-13-01', '2026-04-31' → 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`; '2028-02-29' and '2000-02-29' valid; start '9:00', '24:00', '12:60' → 400 `start must be HH:MM`; end bad → `end must be HH:MM`; end == start and end < start → 400 `end must be after start`; first failing rule wins (bad room AND bad date → room message). 201 body is exactly {id, room, title, date, start, end} (deepEqual), id 1 then 2; extra keys ignored.
7. Rule 10: with Aurora 2026-11-03 10:00-11:00 and 09:00-09:30 booked, POST 09:15-10:30 → 409 `room is already booked from 09:00 to 09:30`; 11:00-12:00 OK (touching); same time in Borealis OK; other date OK.
8. GET /api/bookings sorts by date, start, then room order Aurora < Borealis < Cosmos (insert in reverse order to prove it); ?date=2026-11-03 filters; ?date (no =), ?date= and ?date=bad → 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`; ?date=2026-11-03&date=bad uses the first; ?x=1 ignored.
9. Persistence: create 2, delete id 2, restart server with same DATA_FILE → bookings same, next POST gets id 3. Check the data file parses to {nextId:3,...} before restart and no `.tmp` files remain in the folder.
10. Concurrency: 10 overlapping POSTs at once (Promise.all) → exactly one 201, nine 409; then 10 non-overlapping concurrent POSTs → all 201 with unique ids.
11. Save failure: DATA_FILE = <tmp>/missing-dir/data.json → server starts; POST → 500 `{"error":"internal error"}`; GET shows no bookings; the folder still doesn't exist; then fs.mkdirSync the folder, POST → 201 with id 1 (next id unchanged by the failure).
12. GET / and GET /app.js: if `public/index.html` / `public/app.js` exist, 200 with content-type exactly `text/html; charset=utf-8` / `text/javascript; charset=utf-8`; if missing, t.skip. POST / → 405.

Run `node --test test/` from /root/bench-runs/h4-c3e12a23 and report: pass/fail counts and, for every failure, the test name, expected vs actual. Keep your final message short.

content.content: 1 # Spec (verbatim from the user) — owner: supervisor 2 3 Constraints: Node.js built-ins only (no npm install). Do not use the Fable model. Node v22. 4 5 Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. 6 7 Server 8 - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. 9 - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. 10 - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. 11 - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. 12 - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. 13 - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. 14 - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. 15 - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. 16 - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. 17 - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. 18 19 API 20 - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. 21 - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. 22 - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. 23 - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. 24 - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. 25 - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above.
